<issue>
only do glibc checks on client?
Copying my reply to an issue posted on the mailing list to here:

```
     $ borg init --e none ./borgtest
     Remote: FATAL: this Python was compiled for a too old (g)libc and
     misses required functionality.
```
This is the code which triggers this exception / error message:

```
    required_funcs = {os.stat, os.utime, os.chown}
    if not os.supports_follow_symlinks.issuperset(required_funcs):
        raise PythonLibcTooOld
```

So, as you see, quite basic functionality like not following symlinks is not supported for all function where borg needs that.

So far for the bad news.

The good news are that these functions might be only required for using borg as a client, but not for "borg serve" (repo server part in client/server mode, if repo access is done via ssh:).

borg currently always does this check, but I guess it could be maybe omitted for the "borg serve" server part.
</issue>

149|     module level (and thus executed at import time - BEFORE setup_logging()
150|     was called). By doing it lazily we can do the setup first, we just have to

3| 
4| class LRUCache:
5|     def __init__(self, capacity, dispose):
6|         self._cache = {}
7|         self._lru = []
8|         self._capacity = capacity
9|         self._dispose = dispose
10| 
11|     def __setitem__(self, key, value):
12|         assert key not in self._cache, (
13|             "Unexpected attempt to replace a cached item,"
14|             " without first deleting the old item.")
15|         self._lru.append(key)
16|         while len(self._lru) > self._capacity:
17|             del self[self._lru[0]]
18|         self._cache[key] = value
19| 
20|     def __getitem__(self, key):
21|         value = self._cache[key]  # raise KeyError if not found
22|         self._lru.remove(key)
23|         self._lru.append(key)
24|         return value
25| 
26|     def __delitem__(self, key):
27|         value = self._cache.pop(key)  # raise KeyError if not found
28|         self._dispose(value)
29|         self._lru.remove(key)
30| 
31|     def __contains__(self, key):
32|         return key in self._cache
33| 
34|     def get(self, key, default=None):
35|         value = self._cache.get(key, sentinel)
36|         if value is sentinel:
37|             return default
38|         self._lru.remove(key)
39|         self._lru.append(key)
40|         return value
41| 
42|     def upd(self, key, value):
43|         # special use only: update the value for an existing key without having to dispose it first
44|         # this method complements __setitem__ which should be used for the normal use case.
45|         assert key in self._cache, "Unexpected attempt to update a non-existing item."
46|         self._cache[key] = value
47| 
48|     def clear(self):
49|         for value in self._cache.values():
50|             self._dispose(value)
51|         self._cache.clear()
52| 
53|     def items(self):
54|         return self._cache.items()
55| 
56|     def __len__(self):
57|         return len(self._cache)
